title: Notes of Ministry - 36 - November 1975

source.file: Various/Notes of Ministry - 36 - November 1 (2414)/Notes of Ministry - 36 - Novemb - Various.epub

paragraphs.text: I want to say a brief and simple word about being led, led out—divine leading with the greatest possible objectives in view. I have referred to these scriptures because in them God leads in regard to Abraham, the Lord leads in regard to His own, and I am free to say, the Spirit leads especially in relation to the personnel of the assembly with that sublime relationship in mind that responds feelingly to God—I refer to sonship. I wondered if we could see that this leading by God, in the way in which He has revealed Himself in the economy, is a leading out which necessarily involves a leading away from the things that detain us here into a great spiritual order of things where God can find His own satisfaction at the present time. To me this is wonderfully blessed and a compensating current answer to the sufferings of Jesus that will surely be filled out in a coming day when the myriads of the redeemed, heavenly in their character, will surround Him to the satisfaction of God Himself.

I suppose everybody here realises that the call of God stands related to these things. Do you know that God has called you? I say that because I would like to embrace everyone here, young and old, in these wonderful realities. You are not too young to come into them, and I will tell you why you are not too young. If you had gone along with Abraham as God, so to speak, took him by the hand and led, him out, and if you had looked up to the heavens, you would have seen those myriads of stars. I was speaking to a man who spent six and a half years in the desert in the war and he said to me, ‘You know, the stars are wonderful here, but in the desert, in the stillness of the desert night, especially when there is no moon, the brilliance of the stars is marvellous, wonderful!’. Do you know what marks the stars? When you look up into the heavens I wonder how often people do that—there are little ones and there are bigger ones and together there is a great galaxy of glory. The Scripture says about the stars that they differ, “For star differs from star in glory”, 1 Corinthians 15: 41. So however young you are, if you are a believer in Jesus, however limited you feel (for who does not feel limited in regard to our appreciation of Him?) you can take your place among the stars to shine as a testimony, a heavenly testimony, to what God is doing and will yet do, and presently will display.

God said to Abraham, “Fear not. Abram; I am thy shield, thy exceeding great reward”. That is, protection on the one hand and a reward. You say, what was the reward for? Abraham had responded to God and he had come out of the situation in which he was. God called him, and he answered. The call to Abraham was a call away not only from the world but from nature.

Not that he had not natural things to look after and attend to, he had, and he did it very well because there were trained servants in his house; but he was called out and God says, ‘I will shield and look after you and protect you and I am your “exceeding great reward”, but I want to show you something that is heavenly, Abram’. So He led him out and I believe, beloved brethren, that the matter of being led by God out of what is circumstantial is the surest way to get a glimpse of the glory of what is heavenly. This is what He did—“He led him out, and said, Look now toward the heavens, and number the stars, if thou be able to number them. And he said to him, So shall thy seed be! And he believed Jehovah; and he reckoned it to him as righteousness”.

That is to say there was something there now in Abraham that corresponded with the God who led him out. “He believed Jehovah; and he reckoned it to him as righteousness”. And what was the result? Why, he was occupied with the heavenly side of what God had in mind in the glory. We would say, the glory of the saints—not only as individuals, although each one has his glory but that glory seen as they are set together, which involves features of what the assembly is. I think there is a pointer to the assembly in this heavenly assemblage, for these stars are all different. A man said to me, ‘It is wonderful that there are millions of stars and they are all moving, but none of them collide’. It is wonderful, is it not? So in the assembly all are to move together, beloved, all in relation to Christ, and in such a way that there is perfect accord, even though the personnel are individuals and their experiences are all different.

I do not linger on this, but turn to the Lord’s leading. He led His own out, “He led them out as far as Bethany”. He led them out. He had opened their understandings, He Himself was in resurrection; the work of redemption had been accomplished, the overthrow of death, the victory over the grave, was a finished and a settled matter. If we were to apply the teaching of the gospel as set out by the Holy Spirit through the apostle Paul to the position that existed in Jesus as out of death, we would say that persons who put their confidence in Him were justified before God. Their offences had been dealt with, He had been raised again for their justification (see Romans 4: 25), they were justified before God—that is free in the presence of God. What does He do? Leave them in that religious setting in which, I suppose, they had grown up? Does He leave them there? No, He does not do that! He leads them out to a location, to a place. That place where there is love for Christ, that is Bethany. He Himself moved out from the city that refused Him and found comfort and rest in Bethany. It is a place where love is. I say to my own heart, Do you know it? I say to yours, Do you know it?—A place where Christ is loved; it is where He led them after His resurrection. Oh, they had had their sins forgiven, they knew what it was to be justified through our Lord Jesus Christ, they knew what it was to be justified on the principle of faith, but He led them out. They had not yet the Spirit, but He led them out to this place and I believe that this place to which Jesus led them out is a starting point into the most blessed assembly privileges and one from which the service of God can proceed in the glory and liberty of sonship. It is a starting point, but He led them out. What we are saying is very simple, but I think it is very important. God led Abraham out to view what was heavenly.
You cannot see it if you are occupied with the things of this world. There is a verse we used to sing—

‘Turn your eyes upon Jesus;
Look full in His wonderful face,
And the things of earth will grow strangely dim
In the light of His glory and grace’.
That is right. If you try it you find it out; if you do not try it, you will not find it out.

So Abraham was led out to view what was heavenly. Jesus led them out to Bethany, the place where He was loved, in view of a further move, because He says, “I send the promise of my Father upon you; but do ye remain in the city till ye be clothed with power from on high”. “He led them out”, it says, “as far as Bethany, and having lifted up his hands, he blessed them. And it came to pass as he was blessing them, he was separated from them and was carried up into heaven”. Now, beloved brethren, this is a starting point. Where do you think your destination is? Where else could it be but where Jesus is? The destination is heaven and the Spirit is here with that in view.

In the epistle to the Romans there are people who are led by the Spirit of God. It says, “For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are sons of God”. I think they are led in relation to the greatest and the most glorious matters that are given in God’s grace for people like you and me to have part in. Over against the Spirit is: the flesh. “We are debtors, not to the flesh, to live according to flesh; for if ye live according to flesh, ye are about to die; but if, by the Spirit, ye put to death the deeds of the body, ye shall live”. What does it mean practically, “If, by the Spirit, ye put to death the deeds of the body, ye shall live”? Do you know where our trouble lies? In our members, that is where it lies, and if I want to say or do something or go somewhere that I know is only for the satisfaction of the flesh, the Spirit helps me to say, No.

That is what He helps me to do, and in the doing of it the way lies open for me to enjoy the life that properly belongs to the believer. It is that new kind of life which is normal to the believer in Jesus and is suited to be brought into the assembly. There is pureness of affection and right moral conditions and so He leads. Where does the Spirit lead? He leads, I believe, from this place, this spiritual location, where Christ is loved. He leads into the blessedness of the service of God in the assembly because the service of God is taken up by those who are sons of God. Surely He leads in the testimony, too, and He leads in relation to the truth, but He also leads in relation to this matter of sonship so that there is a response from these persons. As, it says, “For ye have not received a spirit of bondage again for fear, but ye have received a spirit of adoption (or sonship), whereby we cry, Abba, Father”. Nobody cries, ‘Abba, Father’ whose affections are not stirred towards that blessed Person.

How are the affections stirred? By the Spirit. Is there consciousness of this? Of course, because “The Spirit itself bears witness with our spirit, that we are children of God”. We are given the consciousness of the relationship in which we are; He gives us, too, the power to respond, but it is on the principle of being led, and if I am a person who is willing to be led I am one whose will is in subjection. O, dear brethren, how blessed just to be subject; subject to the word, subject to Christ, subject to the Spirit, and we shall find how that makes it relatively easy to be subject to one another. I am sure of this, that the positive engagement with what is available as being led out is the surest way to find liberty in what is going in, what goes back, what is led in. That was what was in God’s mind in regard to His people Israel. He led them out, but Moses, spiritual man that he was, with that long-distance look, said, “Thou shalt bring them in, and plant them in the mountain of thine inheritance ... The Sanctuary, Lord, that thy hands have prepared” (Exodus 15: 17), and Miriam took it up, a subjective answer in the saints.

Beloved, I would like to be identified with this experience; would not you? Are you ready to be led out, or do you want to stay back there? There is no place for Christ out there. You bear testimony to Him, and you will soon find that out! There is no place for Him out there. He would lead you out of that order of things into the heavenly order of things—glorious and blessed portion! He would occupy you with the heavenly glories of the saints, and lead you to a place where He is loved so that you might have part, in the liberty of sonship, in response to Him who is God and Father. May we know it and enjoy it, and may God be served in this wonderful light, for Christ’s sake.
In the beginning of this gospel when the magi were enquiring after the little child, Jesus, they came to Herod and he instructed them to search out where He was and to report back to him.

What we find is that after they had honoured Him they were divinely instructed in a dream not to return to Herod and they departed to their own country another way. I think that is a feature that should be understood by us, dear brethren—this thought of another way—especially in this gospel which, as we have been taught, is the assembly gospel. I thought we might see something from this section of the education the Lord would afford His own in view of their part in the assembly—their functioning in the assembly—how He would instruct them so that something of another way would be known by them.

First of all in Matthew 17 we get a view of the Lord in this glorious setting. The Lord said in the end of chapter 16 that, “There are some of those standing here that shall not taste of death at all until they shall have seen the Son of man coming in his kingdom”. Now that would be the Son of man in glorious surroundings. We are accustomed to think of the Son of man in conditions of humiliation, and that is right. He has been in conditions such as those; but then they were going to get a view of the Son of man coming in His kingdom—the Son of man in His glory, in His glorious surroundings—and from that I think they would learn something that would equip them in view of the part they were going to have in the assembly, because the assembly is a very glorious and very dignified vessel, and I think the presentation of the Son of man coming in His kingdom would help them to understand how they were to have part in this wonderful, dignified vessel, the assembly.

One thing I would like to comment about is how He was transfigured before them—“His face shone as the sun”—I think that would be a beneficent shining. The shining of the sun is beneficent. The Son of man in His kingdom is a matter of divine goodness. It is rule; the sun represents the thought of rule, but it is rule in a beneficent sense. What a thing it is to get a view of Christ in that way, the shining of God beneficently. There is resource connected with the sun; men are trying to harness the power that comes from the sun. I hope to show that the matter of divine resource comes into these scriptures. There are wonderful resources connected with the shining of the sun. What power it radiates, power that is beneficent—“There is nothing hid from the heat thereof” (Psalm 19: 6), the psalmist tells us, and we are conscious of that. As we are in the rays and the shining of the sun we are conscious of something that is beneficent, something that is doing us good.

Along with that, “his garments became white as the light”. That is another feature that would enter into the Son of man coming in His kingdom, the way that God operates in the light. There is nothing obscure, there is no darkness connected with the way that God operates. The Lord would communicate what God is, the outshining of God, God operating in the light.

Now, Peter is there and Peter, like most of us, makes mistakes. I think that is intended to be educational, too, dear brethren, because what it brings out is amenability to adjustment. I think that enters into the matter of understanding something about another way, that we are amenable to being adjusted. If our own way is not going to serve divine ends, then are we going to be amenable to adjustment in the light of another way that the Lord would show us, so that we become serviceable? Peter, I have no doubt at all, got the benefit of the adjustment he received here because in his epistle he speaks about this mountain, and there is nothing about Moses or Elias there; it is just about Christ. “Having, been eyewitnesses of his majesty”, 2 Peter 1: 16. See how Peter had got the point of the adjustment! It was a very fine adjustment here. The Father adjusted Peter by calling attention to Christ, showing His thoughts about Christ. He did not say, ‘You have made, an awful blunder, Peter’; what He did was to call attention to Christ, and in the light, of that Peter got adjustment.

Now, really, I think that is how adjustment comes about with any one of us; we get adjustment in the light of what Christ is. We judge ourselves properly only, I believe, in the light of Christ; so the Father calls attention to Christ, and Peter gets the benefit of the adjustment. What He is saying is, “This is my beloved Son ... hear him”. You might say, Was not Moses a great speaker, did he not have great things to say? Indeed he had, and Elijah, too, could recall the people at a time when things were difficult; but the Lord is providing for difficult situations arising and the thing is, we are to hear Him. There is a need, I believe, if we are to understand something about another way, of hearing Christ, hearing this wonderful Speaker, the Son—Moses and Elijah and every other man must go out of sight when the Son is brought forward. No one can be put in comparison along with Christ; He is incomparable.

Who, indeed, will speak after the Son? There is no speaker like the Son, indeed, it is the speaking of a divine Person Himself in manhood, and so the word is, “Hear him”. You see how the assembly, and assembly persons, are going to be equipped if we have ears to hear what the Son has to say. Peter was amenable to adjustment and I think eventually he would get the benefit of what Christ said, what the Son said. That comes out in Acts and in subsequent history, that Peter had got the benefit of this education.

Coming down from—the mountain they had to meet difficult conditions. There was a case there that the disciples could not meet, and they enquire of the Lord why they could not meet it. Well, that is a good thing to do if we find there is some difficulty that seems insuperable, to enquire of the Lord. They enquired as to the reason and He says, it is “because of your unbelief” (Matthew 17: 20). Then He says, “This kind does not go out but by prayer and fasting” (Matthew 17: 21). I think He just indicated that there was another way. You might say, This method has worked before, but the Lord is saying there is another way this time, and He is indicating the way. You see the benefit of hearing what the Son has to say. He has the answer to the problem.

Then they come to Capernaum, “Those who received the didrachmas came to Peter and said, Does your teacher not pay the didrachmas? He says, Yes”. Peter is saying this without perhaps realising the implications. He is really saying, ‘Christ is just like others, and He pays the didrachmas. He just goes along with what others are doing and He pays the same. If the Jews are doing this, then He will be a good Jew and just do exactly the same’. That is not good enough, because the Son is over the house; He is not under obligation to anyone, and He has something to instil into Peter here that will further his education. It says, “Jesus anticipated him, saying, What dost thou think, Simon? the kings of the earth, from whom do they receive custom or tribute? from their own sons or from strangers?”. You see how He uses the natural idea just to bring the thing home to Peter. So Peter says, “From strangers”, and Jesus says, “Then are the sons free”. He is going to bring Peter into the sense of sonship.

It is the liberty of sonship that He wants to impart to Peter. He is going to have Peter associated with Himself in His thoughts. That is a great matter, dear brethren, because the filling out of the truth of the assembly requires persons in the enjoyment of sonship. It is so great a matter that it requires this, so the Lord is indicating another way to him, the way of sonship, the way of the liberty of sonship. That is a wonderful matter to lay hold of because this is the time of sonship. The epistle to the Galatians greatly enlarges on it. There was a danger of their subscribing to, and returning to, Judaism, and really, in principle, that is just what Peter would have done here, but what the Son was bringing in was infinitely greater than Judaism. Oh to get an impression of what the assembly is, and that it requires for its functioning persons in the enjoyment and liberty of sonship.

Then we have this word which the Lord gives Peter about the fish, “But that we may not be an offence to them, go to the sea and cast a hook, and take the first fish that comes up, and when thou hast opened its mouth thou wilt find a stater; take that and give it to them for me and thee”. Firstly what He does is to make the truth perfectly clear that He is not under obligation to anyone. Then He would give Peter to feel that he was associated with Himself In this great matter of sonship, and you see how divine resource comes in again—the resources of the sea this time, and He can control them. The Lord has control of them, and, if another way is being indicated, then the resources are available to go that other way, to fill it out in sonship. So it is a question of the first fish that comes up. It is not a net; it is just the first fish that comes up and that is going to provide exactly what is needed. How accurate the Lord is in assessing what the need is and bringing in the resource to meet it! I think we arrive at that by the way of sonship.

Then the next touch He gives is as to this little child. They were questioning who was the greatest in the kingdom of the heavens, “And Jesus having called a little child to him, set it in their midst”. He would exemplify the kind of thing He has in mind. You see, He is leading up to this matter of the assembly here. Now, normally, if men have a great conference they look for the most distinctive personages they can find. In christianity they are there in the sons, but then their attitude and their deportment is to be this unassuming character of little children.

Now the Lord exemplifies the kind of thing He will have in the assembly by putting this little child in their midst. We have been reminded that all through this section down to the end of verse 20 there is no reference to this little child going away, as if to imply that it was there during that time. Hence while He was speaking about this wonderful, august vessel, the assembly, and the part they were going to have in it, the spirit and character of things that are to mark it would be exemplified in this little child.

We carry these thoughts forward, dear brethren, in our minds in what the Lord says from verse 15 onwards. He says, “But if thy brother sin against thee, go, reprove him between thee and him alone”. It should be noted that it is “thy brother”. Your brother is a very valuable person when it comes to the truth of the assembly. You need someone with you to work out the truth of the assembly. One person on his own cannot work it out. He needs somebody else along with him—“thy brother”. It is a wonderful matter to appreciate the feelings of divine Persons in relation to this. The Lord has spoken just earlier about the Son of man coming to save that which was lost (verse 11). He speaks about a man having a hundred sheep and one going astray and how he would go after it to find it, and then He speaks about the will of the Father—“It is not the will of your Father ... that one of these little ones should perish” (Matthew 18: 14). How the disposition and attitude of divine Persons are brought in, conveyed to us in the Son of man, conveyed to us in the Father in His will. Then there is a person who is valuable because he has been the subject of divine operations. Oh to get a view of a brother in that light!—not just an offender but “if thy brother sin against thee”. So He says, “Go, reprove him between thee and him alone”. Give him all the advantage you can; put him in the most advantageous position you can. That is what the Lord is saying. Then, “If he hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother”. It is a wonderful thing that a brother should be gained. It is not the divine intent that persons should be lost. That is the whole spirit and attitude of this approach, involving the Son of man coming to save, and the Father’s will. You would glean from that that the idea of loss is not what is in mind. The idea of gain is in mind, that a brother should be gained.

Then, “If he do not hear thee, take with thee one or two besides, that every matter may stand upon the word of two witnesses or of three”. There is a measure of grace in one going, but that may not be sufficient. Therefore additional grace in two or three is brought to bear upon the brother and then, if that is not effective, “If he will not listen to them, tell it to the assembly”. The assembly is the great vessel of divine grace. Thus you have grace in a brother, then in two or three, but the greatest expression of divine grace you can have in the saints is in this wonderful vessel, the assembly. What would be in mind is the securing of the brother. It may be that he will not listen. Well, there is provision for that—“If also he will not listen to the assembly ...”. That is a very serious thing if someone will not listen to the vessel that is the great expression of divine grace. It may be that that could be so, but I think that the whole intention of this scripture is that a brother should be gained, and the arrangement is in view of that. Hence the resources of heaven are brought in in connection with this wonderful vessel.

It implies the dignity and order that belong to this vessel. It implies on the one hand the spirit of the little child, the unassuming, inoffensive spirit that the Lord would have characterise the assembly, and on the other it involves the dignity of persons who know something about sonship, who know something about being associated with Christ. The assembly is a vessel of divine order and wonderful dignity, the most august vessel in the universe. It might come that the assembly has to act in the way of withdrawal, of exclusion. That would be a very solemn thing and that would be the last resort. The last thing you would do, we have been taught, is to withdraw from a brother, the very last thing you would do. If all the resources of divine grace are ineffective, you might have to do that. If it were a matter of public dishonour to the Lord’s name, you might have to do that, but otherwise the resources of divine grace are brought to bear, all the resources there are in this wonderful vessel, dear brethren. Then if it had to come to the point where a brother had to be withdrawn from, you would have to say, ‘We could do no more’—if it came to that point. Then the Lord goes on to say, “Whatsoever ye shall bind on the earth shall be bound in heaven, and whatsoever ye shall loose on the earth shall be loosed in heaven”. So that becomes a very serious consideration as to anything we do in the light of the assembly. I do not say we act as the assembly, dear brethren, but the only light we can act in is the light of the assembly, unassumingly, in the spirit of the little child; but if we do act in that light, it becomes a serious consideration as to whether heaven can ratify what is done. One thing to keep in mind is the shining that is proper to this vessel.

The disciples saw the One whose face shone as the sun, and there is the shining of the assembly. John got a view of the assembly in her shining—he saw the holy city, Jerusalem, coming down out of the heaven from God, having the glory of God (Revelation 21: 10), coming down to bring the influence of heaven to bear upon the millennial world, a vessel capable of bringing the influence of heaven to bear upon the earth below. That is the vessel we have to do with. That is the vessel we are part of. That is the vessel the Lord is speaking about here, although in different circumstances, dear brethren. What is said about her, “Her shining was like a most precious stone, as a crystal-like jasper stone” (Revelation 21: 11), means that things are crystal-clear, you see; there is no cloudiness, no haziness, there is no ambiguity, everything is clear. It is morally in keeping with the One whose garments were white as the light. That is how it is to be in divine administration.

What I just want to touch on in closing is that there are other resources. The administrative and executive resource is not all that the assembly has. We have been taught that the assembly is never driven to the wall. The Lord says, “Again I say to you, that if two of you shall agree on the earth concerning any matter, whatsoever it may be that they shall ask, it shall come to them from my Father who is in the heavens” Is that not a wonderful thing—something coming from the Father who is in the heavens because of persons down here asking? And it is brought into the context of the latter days, our days—“Again I say to you”. You may say, How is this workable in a day when publicly everything has gone to the wall? The Lord says, “Again I say to you”. Things are coming down to just two or three, and heaven is interested; the Father who is in the heavens is interested. Is that not a real resource? You might say, ‘We could not do anything else but take executive action’, but the Lord might say, ‘There is another way’. Perhaps there may be another way, by which we can make way for the resources of heaven by asking, using the power of prayer. The resources of heaven are brought into view. He says, “For where two or three are gathered together unto my name, there am I in the midst of them”. There is nothing given up of what belongs to His name. His name is honoured; but the Father is brought in, and heaven is brought in, and there is something coming from the Father who is in the heavens in response to the power of prayer in the saints. So it is coming right down to this matter of two or three—“For where two or three are gathered together unto my name, there am I in the midst of them”. How He would mark off persons with this dignity, “in the midst of them”—assembly persons, so valuable to heaven!

I think the matter lies, dear brethren, in hearing the Lord, in making way for the resources of heaven, in being ready for adjustment in the way the Lord would indicate—and if we are amenable to His indications we find that the Lord can work something out in this wonderful sphere which He has—the assembly. I feel greatly challenged in myself by what I am saying, but just pass on the thoughts humbly, and trust that the Lord may bless the word.

I would like to say something, beloved brethren, about the value of leadership and eldership in the protection of the saints. I am conscious of inability to speak of it, but just seek to convey an impression which is bearing upon me as to its importance.

Leadership in Psalm 77 is very significant, referring to Moses and Aaron. When you think of the number of souls that had to be guided, having crossed the Red Sea, through the wilderness, with a view to taking up their possession in the land which God had prepared for them, what a commission they had! What impresses me about this leadership is that it is a single hand, the hand of Moses and Aaron. There would be something distinctive in that, I feel sure. We have been taught that Moses relates to what is authoritative and Aaron to what is priestly, yet it is one hand. It raises the enquiry with me as to where did they join hand? I suggest they joined hand when they met in Exodus.4—on the mountain of God. Oh what a thing it is to see that side of things, what is authoritative and what is priestly joining together and embracing at the height of the mountain of God! You feel the significance of what is brotherly in relation to what is authoritative and what is priestly, as bearing on the leadership of the saints. The separation of these things can lead to disaster.

The flock, as it is spoken of in each of these scriptures, impresses me. This would be something that is sensitive, something that is worthy of protection and needs protection. Let us gather the impression that the work of God in the saints in localities needs protection and is worthy of protection. Leadership is therefore necessary. We have come through much under an authoritative leadership involving legality but, beloved brethren, the feature of leadership is still necessary for the leading of God’s people in a broken day. I would like to discern what corresponds to “the hand of Moses and Aaron” today in the maintenance of what is authoritative in relation to the truth in every locality, yet operating in a priestly way.

This will be found as we join hands in brotherliness, flowing from affections formed in the atmosphere of the mountain of God. This influence is then brought to bear on how we lead God’s people forward in a right way. Leadership for the children of Israel was essential if they were to reach their portion in Canaan. Six hundred thousand men, besides children, were claimed from Egypt and step by step their wilderness journey had to be trod. What a hand this had to be! This was leadership by the influence of what is authoritative and priestly and would set a divine pattern for God’s people down to our day. Let us realise that these features are necessary in every locality for the protection of the work of God in the saints.

So we can each raise the question—with, ourselves first—What course am I on? What course are the saints on? Is it a course that is away from the world and leading ever towards heaven? Leadership would come into that; leadership is to influence the saints in the direction of what is their heavenly portion. O beloved brethren, to be on this line! You could quote the failure of Aaron, and you could quote other things, but oh to look over the history and discern the leading by the hand of Moses and Aaron of this people like a flock. Leadership is necessary, but let it afresh flow from the merging of what is authoritative and what is priestly as having been formed together in brotherly links emanating from the atmosphere of the mountain of God.

So as to eldership, Peter is appealing in his epistle. We have been taught that the function of eldership would be particularly local. Titus having been instructed to establish elders in each city, Titus 1: 5. Think of the language of Peter, “The elders which are among you, I exhort”. It is in view of service as appreciating that there is something there worth protecting and worth serving, not for a name for themselves, but all in view of the “unfading crown of glory”. What an appreciation, what a glory, comes out in that, “when the chief shepherd is manifested”. Let us contemplate afresh the language of Peter, “Shepherd the flock of God”. Oh to be able to do that! The footnote is most interesting, and may we become that way, actively doing the thing, ‘Be shepherders’ of “the flock of God”, as realising there is something worth protecting. We think of the encouragement this week of a young one asking to remember the Lord, the work of God coming to light in younger persons.

It all enforces the responsibility of protecting what is according to God locally. Eldership would come out that way. We have not many elder brothers here, hence the need for every one of us to commit ourselves to this service. But O beloved brethren, let us do it, and let us commit ourselves to it as seeing that there is something worthy of protection. Think of it from that viewpoint. So Peter speaks of himself as a “witness of the sufferings of the Christ”, and he brings all the force and weight of that to bear upon the elders, who needed encouraging to shepherd the flock of God.

We may think of Jesus on the cross committing His mother to John. The Lord in this way sets the matter on with His on example, “And from that hour the disciple took her to his on home”, John 19: 27. These things are there, beloved brethren, for our contemplation as the Lord Jesus cares for what is worthy because it is according to God. Oh let us value the work of God that is there in all its purity and extensiveness amongst the saints, and let us see that it requires protection.

So in Acts 20 Paul encourages the elders likewise to “shepherd the assembly of God, which he has purchased with the blood of his own”. What a lever Paul brings, like Peter, into this exercise. Having called over the elders of Ephesus he brings the whole weight of his personal appreciation of the assembly, and of the work of God in the saints who compose it, to bear upon the elders, encouraging them to shepherd, and to watch, as realising there is something worthy of protection and worthy to be served.

Oh I would love to be more in it and to be more convicted as to it, and to be able to encourage the brethren more on this line of valuing what is local and valuing what is in every brother and sister as seeing there is something worthy of protection, because, beloved brethren, the true place for the work of God is to be housed in heaven. And you find that work in your local brother; in the brother next to you, or the sister next to you, or in the combination of the local meeting as you look round and see the work of God in the saints, right down to younger ones, and realise your responsibility to protect it, to lead it, to have your own part in leading and influencing the saints afresh toward the heavenly portion and toward a calling that is not for this world, but for that world, where Christ is the Head and Centre. May we be encouraged in these things, for His name’s sake.

In Solomon’s temple there were ten lavers of brass, each holding forty baths; these lavers were on wheels, thus corresponding to what the Lord used here (John 13), as they could be carried and moved. On the one hand there was plenty of water for the needs of those who were exercised to be there according to God’s thoughts (I am referring to the molten sea), and on the other hand there was water in the brass lavers for the service of the saints … It is a clear witness to the death of Christ, so that no one need be unclean or defiled. The molten sea remained permanently in its place; but the lavers of brass could be moved in love towards the one needing help or purification; they indicate the opportunity which is given to us to serve one another in love. They were magnificently ornamented, showing how one moving in this way in love is beautified.

It is quite possible for us to pray while lying in bed; the psalmist records how he arose in the night to give thanks to God. During the night watches we can turn to God in prayer, while lying on our beds, and He hears us. To pray for the saints is one of the most important services that can be rendered, and those who are laid aside can devote themselves to this service.

In everything I do, I am under obligation to my brethren locally and generally, as if each member of the association informed the others of what he is doing so that they could participate. Hence, if I am honest, my conscience will not permit me to do anything when my brethren are not looking, that I would not do when they are looking for I involve them in all I do … All those breaking bread form part of the association, as we all partake of one loaf.
